title: NodePool Units + Burst Credits: packaging experiment and enterprise SQ playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Propose a new packaging model for Dedicated capacity that decouples long-term reserved GPU commitments from short-term burst capacity and autoscale prewarm behavior. Key primitives: NodePool Units (NPU) as the subscription object for reserved throughput, Burst Credits (BC) for short-term surges, and Prewarm Tokens (PT) to reduce cold-start tail latency. This ticket captures the experiment design, pricing matrix drafts, enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) response templates, and rollout gating criteria. Goals: 1) Increase conversion of mid-market customers from hosted -> Dedicated by 12% in Q2; 2) Reduce churn for new Dedicated customers in first 90 days by 20% through softer entry points (low NPU minimum + purchasable BC); 3) Maintain gross margin on Dedicated offers above 55% through tailored per-NPU pricing + burst premium. Pricing primitives: - NPU: baseline unit representing a pool of GPU capacity equivalent (example: 1 NPU ~= 1x A10-equivalent reserved slice for 1 vCPU ratio). Charged monthly as subscription. Volume tiers and discounts apply. - Burst Credits (BC): prepaid token packs that allow short-lived overcommit beyond reserved NPUs. Sold in 10/50/200 packs with decreasing per-credit price. Unused BC expire monthly. - Prewarm Tokens (PT): one-time or recurring purchase that guarantees pre-populated KV cache/warm containers on a fraction of the pool to reduce tail latency for cold starts. Offered as add-on tiers (none / standard / guaranteed). - Overage/auto-borrow: allow short automatic borrowing of BC when bursts exceed balance with configurable cap and true-up invoice. Experiment variants: A) Self-serve NPU with mandatory 1-month min, BC optional B) Sales-assisted starter: 3-month NPU at discounted rate + BC bundle C) Low-commit trial: 0.5 NPU equivalent for 30 days with PT trial. Metrics and success criteria: - Activation: % of signups who configure NPU + BC within first 7 days. Target 40% for sales-assisted, 25% for self-serve. - Revenue: ARR attributable to new packaging vs control cohort after 90 days. Target +15% ARR per new customer. - SLOs: Maintain average 95th latency within SLA for Gold tier when BC used. - Churn: first-90-day churn reduction of 20% vs historical. Experiment timeline: Week 0-2: finalize price bands and compute iso-cost points vs existing reserved SKU Week 3-4: implement front-end surfaces + billing flags in Console (canary in single region) Week 5-8: run A/B test with 30% traffic allocation; parallel sales pilot with top 10 existing prospects Week 9: evaluate metrics, finance/legal signoff, decide rollout. Financial modeling ask: Finance to provide sensitivity curves for price elasticity and margin at NPU price points: baseline $X/month, mid-discount -15%, enterprise -30%. Include scenario for BC uptake rates from 5% to 60% of traffic. Enterprise SQ and contract implications: - Required SQ sections drafted: data residency, KMS/HSM key management, audit log retention and access, vulnerability disclosure and patch cadence, maintenance windows and upgrade SLAs, private control plane architecture and zero-trust network options. - Proposed standardized responses and optional attachments: a) KMS options: customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) via AWS KMS / GCP CMEK / Azure Key Vault; HSM-backed key for Platinum SLA b) Audit logs: retention choices 30/90/365 days; export via secure syslog or S3 c) Maintenance windows: suggested default 2-hour weekly window with optional 24/7-ops premium d) Upgrade controls: customer can opt into manual approval for major runtime upgrades (enterprise cadence) - Sales playbook snippets and objection handling for SQ items included in comments. Rollout guards and risk mitigation: - Cap initial exposure to <5% of total Dedicated capacity to limit margin risk - Auto-fallback: if BC borrow exceeds threshold, routing policy should fall back to compatible hosted model variant to preserve SLAs - Monitoring: dedicated dashboard for NPU/BC utilization, BC exhaustion rate, prewarm hit-rate, and revenue leakage signals - Legal: require explicit opt-in for auto-borrow and clear invoice line-items for BC usage Implementation dependencies: - Billing pipeline change to support BC packs, expiry, and true-up invoice line-items - Console UI surfaces for configuring NPU/BC/PT and purchase flows - Runtime changes for prewarm token reservation and eviction policy - Contract templating for new SLA tiers and add-on PT language
